meta.description: Character LoRA on IllustriousXL (SDXL arch) for a 16GB laptop GPU. Recipe values (rank 32/alpha 32 + conv 16/16, adamw8bit, LR 1e-4, 1024 training resolution) are UNCHANGED from illustriousxl_character_lora. The point of this variant is batch discipline: this preset keeps batch 1 and reaches an effective batch of 2 via gradient_accumulation 2, trading wall-clock for VRAM. Effective batch 2, not 4: the step suggestion divides by effective batch, and at 4 that quotient drops under the arch's step floor on any small/medium dataset, gets clamped back up, and silently inflates real per-image exposure 2-3x past target - the advisor then recommends a step count its own exposure gauge would flag as fry-risk. The advisor's Illustrious recipe now also recommends batch 2, so the two agree; it remains VRAM-unaware, so on this machine reach effective batch through accumulation as configured here rather than raising batch size. Note the advisor also suggests a HIGHER LR for Illustrious (2e-4 small / 3e-4 otherwise) than the 1e-4 inherited here, and its optimizer choice is genuinely contested in the source guides (adamw8bit + constant vs Prodigy + cosine) - those are recipe questions, unaffected by this hardware profile, and are left exactly as the parent preset had them. Other deltas: low_vram true, cache_latents true alongside cache_latents_to_disk so latents are served from RAM rather than re-read and deep-copied from disk every step (native Windows runs the dataloader at num_workers 0), and ui_db_poll_seconds 2 to throttle the UI's per-step sqlite polling (cost: up to 2s of latency on the stop/save-now buttons). Left unquantized like the parent, holding quantization in reserve as an OOM lever. NOT measured on 16GB hardware. Point model.name_or_path at your local Illustrious checkpoint if you have one. Use booru-style tag captions with a unique trigger tag first. If you swap the optimizer to an Automagic variant, this batch-1-plus-accumulation pattern will not work as-is - Automagic fuses its step into the backward pass by default, so gradient_accumulation must go back to 1 and the effective batch reached by raising batch size instead.
